493: .orchestra/LESSONS.md
494: 1: # Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)
495: 2: 
496: 3: Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.
497: 4: 
498: 5: 1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
499: 6:    predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
500: 7: 2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
501: 8:    volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
502: 9: 3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
503: 10:    that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
504: 11: 4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
505: 12:    to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
506: 13: 5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
507: 14:    input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
508: 15: 6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
509: 16:    (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
510: 17: 7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
511: 18:    carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
512: 19: 8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
513: 20:    so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
514: 21:    (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
515: 22: 9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
516: 23:    ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
517: 24:    multicomponent cells can be used.
518: 25: 10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
519: 26:     candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
520: 27:     fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
521: 28: 11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
522: 29:     energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
523: 30: 12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
524: 31:     from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
525: 32:     GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
526: 33:     0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
527: 34:     (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
528: 35: 13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
529: 36:     response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).
530: 37: 
531: 38: 14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
532: 39:     at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
533: 40:     gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
534: 41:     which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
535: 42:     Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
536: 43:     design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.

669: 52: def kp(alloy, x, v):

976: 36: def site_counts(comp: dict[str, float], n: int) -> dict[str, int]:
977: 37:     counts = {el: int(round(x * n)) for el, x in comp.items()}
978: 38:     counts[max(counts, key=counts.get)] += n - sum(counts.values())

982: 42: def actual_fractions(atoms: Atoms) -> dict[str, float]:
983: 43:     """Composition the cell really has. Subtract pure references with these, not the nominal fractions (the
984: 44:     rounding to whole atoms shifted E_mix by up to ~57 meV/atom before 2026-10-31)."""
985: 45:     s = atoms.get_chemical_symbols()
986: 46:     return {el: s.count(el) / len(s) for el in sorted(set(s))}

989: 49: def solid_solution(comp: dict[str, float], lattice: str, reps: int, seed: int) -> Atoms:
990: 50:     """Random solid solution on a cubic conventional supercell (no SQS optimisation). Counts are rounded to whole
991: 51:     atoms; use actual_fractions() for references."""
992: 52:     a = sum(x * A0[lattice].get(el, 3.5 if lattice == "fcc" else 3.1) for el, x in comp.items())
993: 53:     atoms = bulk("X", lattice, a=a, cubic=True).repeat((reps, reps, reps))
994: 54:     counts = site_counts(comp, len(atoms))
995: 55:     symbols = [el for el, c in counts.items() for _ in range(c)]
996: 56:     np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle(symbols)
997: 57:     atoms.set_chemical_symbols(symbols)
998: 58:     return atoms

1017: 77: def elastic_tensor(atoms: Atoms, eps: float = 0.005, relax_ions: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
1018: 78:     """Full 6x6 Voigt tensor (GPa) from central differences of stress, ions relaxed at each strain."""
1019: 79:     cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
1020: 80:     C = np.zeros((6, 6))
1021: 81:     voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]
1022: 82:     for j, (k, l) in enumerate(voigt):
1023: 83:         sig = []
1024: 84:         for s in (+eps, -eps):
1025: 85:             e = np.zeros((3, 3))
1026: 86:             if k == l:
1027: 87:                 e[k, k] = s
1028: 88:             else:
1029: 89:                 e[k, l] = e[l, k] = s / 2  # engineering shear strain = s
1030: 90:             strained = atoms.copy()
1031: 91:             strained.set_cell(cell0 @ (np.eye(3) + e), scale_atoms=True)
1032: 92:             strained.calc = calculator()
1033: 93:             if relax_ions and len(strained) > 1:
1034: 94:                 relax(strained, cell=False, fmax=5e-4)
1035: 95:             sig.append(strained.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA)  # ASE: tensile stress positive
1036: 96:         C[:, j] = (sig[0] - sig[1]) / (2 * eps)
1037: 97:     return 0.5 * (C + C.T)

1042: 1: """Power check for a pre-registered test, run before the test data exist.
1043: 2: 
1044: 3: A test is only informative if (a) data generated with the hypothesis TRUE, at realistic noise, pass it most of the
1045: 4: time and (b) data with the hypothesis FALSE rarely pass. Both are estimated by simulation. Two failures this tool is
1046: 5: meant to catch, from 2026-10-31: the L3 ordered-cell design (an intercept absorbed the rule's main signal) and R3
1047: 6: (the observable compared relaxed with clamped volumes, so even the exact formula had slope 0.20).
1048: 7: """

1053: 12: 
1054: 13: import numpy as np

1057: 16: def power(test: Callable[[object], bool], simulate_true: Callable[[np.random.Generator], object],
1058: 17:           simulate_null: Callable[[np.random.Generator], object], n: int = 300, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
1059: 18:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
1060: 19:     p = np.mean([bool(test(simulate_true(rng))) for _ in range(n)])
1061: 20:     f = np.mean([bool(test(simulate_null(rng))) for _ in range(n)])
1062: 21:     return {"power": round(float(p), 3), "false_pass": round(float(f), 3), "n_sims": n}

Seed deviations are uncorrelated between channels (r -0.02), so the noise is not the floor. Every target script (k_shear_transfer.py, k44_cofree.py, k_aniso_fresh.py) uses solid_solution(..., seed=0) only, while the rule uses 3-seed binary means. 1634: 46: # Pre-registration and verdicts. A test is registered with its measured power (harness/power.py): a design in which
1635: 47: # a correct formula usually fails is not a test. A failed test is closed with a cause; only cause "hypothesis" retires
1636: 48: # the candidate, "design" and "numerics" send it back to the queue.

1640: 52: def register(claim: str, script: str, power: dict, notes: str = "") -> dict:
1641: 53:     if power.get("power", 0) < 0.8 or power.get("false_pass", 1) > 0.05:
1642: 54:         raise ValueError(f"underpowered or leaky test design, not registered: {power}")
1643: 55:     return record(claim, "L0", [script], notes=f"prereg; power {power}; {notes}".strip("; "))
1644: 56: 
1645: 57: 
1646: 58: def verdict(prereg: str, outcome: str, cause: str, audit: str, evidence: list[str]) -> dict:
1647: 59:     assert cause in CAUSES, cause

1649: 61:         raise ValueError("retiring a candidate needs a post-fail audit (what was checked, by whom)")
1650: 62:     return record(f"verdict on {prereg}: {outcome}", "L0", evidence, notes=f"cause={cause}; audit: {audit}")

FILE scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py
1: """Does the K' volume transfer hold with k = 1 under a second model? Equivalence test (Astra, audit of 6bc0e190a8).
2: 
3: python scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py
4: omat gives k 1.08 twice. mpa gave 1.33 (86767e478d, seed-0 targets and binaries) and then 1.10 [0.94, 1.26] on 150
5: leak-free alloys (unregistered). Here, under medium-mpa-0: 1200 new compositions, 200 in each stratum Co yes/no x
6: 3/4/5 elements, two target cells each (seeds 10000 + 2i, + 1); two independent binary panels (seeds 20-22 and
7: 23-25, the k_shear_transfer.py grid). Cross-panel estimator, so binary noise does not bias k:
8:   k = sum[T_A (y - p_B) + T_B (y - p_A)] / (2 sum T_A T_B),  y = mean of the two cells.
9: CI by bootstrap over compositions and over binary seeds within each panel.
10: PASS (practical equivalence): the 90% CI lies inside [0.90, 1.10]. Reported: the 95% CI and whether it excludes 1.
11: """
12: 
13: import datetime as dt
14: import os
15: import sys
16: import time
17: from pathlib import Path
18: 
19: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
20: os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-mpa-0"
21: sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
22: 
23: import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
24: import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
25: from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402
26: from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline  # noqa: E402
27: 
28: from harness import compute, ledger  # noqa: E402
29: from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402
30: from harness.context import context  # noqa: E402
31: from harness.features import parse_comp  # noqa: E402
32: 
33: assert compute.MODEL == "medium-mpa-0"
34: AMPS = np.array([-0.01, -0.005, 0.0, 0.005, 0.01])
35: GRID = [-0.40, -0.30, -0.20, -0.15, -0.10, -0.05, 0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40]
36: PANELS = {"A": (20, 21, 22), "B": (23, 24, 25)}
37: BIN, TGT = ROOT / "data" / "k_mpa_equiv_binaries.csv", ROOT / "data" / "k_mpa_equiv_targets.csv"
38: ELS = ["Ag", "Au", "Co", "Cu", "Ir", "Ni", "Pd", "Pt", "Rh"]
39: N = 108
40: ctx = context()
41: calc = compute.calculator()
42: SCRIPT = str(Path(__file__))
43: CLAIM = "K' transfer k = 1 under medium-mpa-0"
44: 
45: 
46: def e_strained(atoms, v_atom, F):
47:     a = atoms.copy()
48:     a.set_cell(a.cell * (v_atom * len(a) / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
49:     a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
50:     a.calc = calc
51:     t = time.perf_counter()
52:     e = a.get_potential_energy() / len(a)
53:     time.sleep(time.perf_counter() - t)  # 50% duty cycle, keeps the laptop cool
54:     return e
55: 
56: 
57: def kp(alloy, x, v):
58:     pures = {el: bulk(el, "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True) for el in x}
59:     F = lambda s: np.diag([np.exp(s), np.exp(-s), 1.0])  # noqa: E731
60:     em = [e_strained(alloy, v, F(s)) - sum(xi * e_strained(pures[el], v, F(s)) for el, xi in x.items()) for s in AMPS]
61:     return np.polyfit(AMPS, em, 2)[0] / 2 / v * GPA
62: 
63: 
64: seen = set()
65: for f in ROOT.glob("data/*.csv"):
66:     if "sealed" in str(f):
67:         continue
68:     try:
69:         h = pd.read_csv(f, nrows=0).columns
70:         col = "comp_actual" if "comp_actual" in h else "comp" if "comp" in h else None
71:         if col:
72:             seen |= set(pd.read_csv(f, usecols=[col])[col].astype(str))
73:     except Exception:
74:         pass
75: 
76: 
77: def draw(rng, k, with_co):
78:     while True:
79:         pool = [e for e in ELS if e != "Co"]
80:         els = sorted([*rng.choice(pool, k - 1, replace=False), "Co"] if with_co else rng.choice(pool, k, replace=False))
81:         cnt = 11 + rng.multinomial(N - 11 * k, rng.dirichlet(np.ones(k)))
82:         c = {e: n / N for e, n in zip(els, cnt)}
83:         s = ";".join(f"{e}:{c[e]:.4f}" for e in sorted(c))
84:         if s not in seen:
85:             seen.add(s)
86:             return s, c
87: 
88: 
89: rng = np.random.default_rng(20261103)
90: comps = [draw(rng, k, co) for co in (False, True) for k in (3, 4, 5) for _ in range(200)]
91: C = [c for _, c in comps]
92: PAIRS = sorted({(a, b) for c in C for a, b, _, _ in ctx.pairs(c)})
93: # flattened pair terms over compositions: composition index, pair index, weight 4 x_i x_j, ln V0/V_ij
94: TI, TP, TW, TD = (np.array(v) for v in zip(*[(i, PAIRS.index((a, b)), 4 * xa * xb,
95:                                               np.log(ctx.vegard(c) / ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]))
96:                                              for i, c in enumerate(C) for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c)]))
97: 
98: 
99: def predict(curves):
100:     """curves: (n_pairs, len(GRID)) -> (rule, pair-at-V_ij) over compositions."""
101:     at, at0 = np.empty(len(TI)), np.empty(len(TI))
102:     for p in range(len(PAIRS)):
103:         m = TP == p
104:         if m.any():
105:             sp = CubicSpline(GRID, curves[p])
106:             at[m], at0[m] = sp(TD[m]), sp(0.0)
107:     return np.bincount(TI, TW * at, len(C)), np.bincount(TI, TW * at0, len(C))
108: 
109: 
110: def khat(y, A, B):
111:     (rA, pA), (rB, pB) = A, B
112:     TA, TB = rA - pA, rB - pB
113:     return float((TA @ (y - pB) + TB @ (y - pA)) / (2 * TA @ TB))
114: 
115: 
116: def ci(y, curvesA, curvesB, n_boot, seed):
117:     """curvesX: array (3 seeds, n_pairs, len(GRID)). Bootstrap compositions and seeds within each panel."""
118:     r = np.random.default_rng(seed)
119:     ks = []
120:     for _ in range(n_boot):
121:         A = predict(curvesA[r.integers(0, 3, 3)].mean(0))
122:         B = predict(curvesB[r.integers(0, 3, 3)].mean(0))
123:         i = r.integers(0, len(y), len(y))
124:         ks.append(khat(y[i], (A[0][i], A[1][i]), (B[0][i], B[1][i])))
125:     return np.percentile(ks, [5, 95]), np.percentile(ks, [2.5, 97.5])
126: 
127: 
128: regs = [e for e in ledger.entries() if e["claim"].startswith(CLAIM) and "prereg" in e["notes"]]
129: if not regs:
130:     # Power with the old mpa seed-0 binaries as the "true" curves: target scatter about the rule 2.36 GPa (150-alloy
131:     # residual, 6bc0e190a8), halved in variance by two cells; binary seed scatter of K' 0.71 GPa per seed (S2 audit).
132:     g = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "binary_kgrid_mpa.csv")
133:     true = np.array([g[g.pair == f"{a}-{b}"].sort_values("dlnV").Kp.values for a, b in PAIRS])
134:     rt, pt = predict(true)
135:     r2 = np.random.default_rng(8)
136: 
137:     def sim(k):
138:         y = pt + k * (rt - pt) + r2.normal(0, 2.36 / np.sqrt(2), len(C))
139:         cA = true[None] + r2.normal(0, 0.71, (3, *true.shape))
140:         cB = true[None] + r2.normal(0, 0.71, (3, *true.shape))
141:         lo, hi = ci(y, cA, cB, 100, int(r2.integers(1 << 30)))[0]
142:         return 0.90 <= lo and hi <= 1.10
143: 
144:     power, fp = float(np.mean([sim(1.0) for _ in range(60)])), float(np.mean([sim(1.15) for _ in range(60)]))
145:     print(f"n {len(C)}, power {power:.3f}, false pass (k 1.15) {fp:.3f}", flush=True)
146:     reg = ledger.register(f"{CLAIM}: on {len(C)} new compositions (Co yes/no x 3/4/5 elements, 200 each, two cells) "
147:                           f"with two independent mpa binary panels, the cross-panel k of the K' volume-transfer rule "
148:                           f"has a 90% CI inside [0.90, 1.10]", SCRIPT, {"power": power, "false_pass": fp},
149:                           notes="Astra audit of 6bc0e190a8; old mpa k 1.33 (86767e478d), leak-free 150 alloys 1.10")
150:     print("registered", reg["id"], flush=True)
151:     regs = [reg]
152: 
153: done = set(map(tuple, pd.read_csv(BIN)[["pair", "seed", "dlnV"]].astype(str).values)) if BIN.exists() else set()
154: for A, B in PAIRS:
155:     for seed in PANELS["A"] + PANELS["B"]:
156:         alloy = compute.solid_solution({A: 0.5, B: 0.5}, "fcc", reps=3, seed=seed)
157:         x = compute.actual_fractions(alloy)
158:         for d in GRID:
159:             if (f"{A}-{B}", str(seed), str(d)) in done:
160:                 continue
161:             v = ctx.pair[(A, B)]["V"] * np.exp(d)
162:             pd.DataFrame([{"pair": f"{A}-{B}", "seed": seed, "dlnV": d, "Kp": kp(alloy, x, v)}]).to_csv(
163:                 BIN, mode="a", header=not BIN.exists(), index=False)
164:     print("binary", A, B, flush=True)
165: 
166: done = set(map(tuple, pd.read_csv(TGT)[["comp", "cell"]].values)) if TGT.exists() else set()
167: for i, (s, c) in enumerate(comps):
168:     for cell in (0, 1):
169:         if (s, cell) in done:
170:             continue
171:         alloy = compute.solid_solution(c, "fcc", reps=3, seed=10000 + 2 * i + cell)
172:         x = compute.actual_fractions(alloy)
173:         pd.DataFrame([{"comp": s, "cell": cell, "co": c.get("Co", 0.0), "n_el": len(c),
174:                        "Kp": kp(alloy, x, ctx.vegard(c)), "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}]
175:                      ).to_csv(TGT, mode="a", header=not TGT.exists(), index=False)
176: print("equiv targets done", flush=True)
177: 
178: b = pd.read_csv(BIN)
179: curves = {p: np.array([[b[(b.pair == f"{x}-{z}") & (b.seed == s)].sort_values("dlnV").Kp.values for x, z in PAIRS]
180:                        for s in PANELS[p]]) for p in PANELS}
181: t = pd.read_csv(TGT).groupby("comp").Kp.mean()
182: y = t.loc[[s for s, _ in comps]].values
183: A, B = predict(curves["A"].mean(0)), predict(curves["B"].mean(0))
184: k = khat(y, A, B)
185: (l90, h90), (l95, h95) = ci(y, curves["A"], curves["B"], 2000, 0)
186: ok = 0.90 <= l90 and h90 <= 1.10
187: print(f"k {k:.3f}, 90% CI [{l90:.3f}, {h90:.3f}], 95% CI [{l95:.3f}, {h95:.3f}] -> {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}; "
188:       f"95% CI {'excludes' if not l95 <= 1 <= h95 else 'contains'} 1", flush=True)
189: for lab, m in (("Co-free", np.array([c.get("Co", 0) == 0 for c in C])), ("Co", np.array([c.get("Co", 0) > 0 for c in C]))):
190:     print(f"  {lab}: k {khat(y[m], (A[0][m], A[1][m]), (B[0][m], B[1][m])):.3f}", flush=True)
191: ledger.record(f"{CLAIM}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} (k {k:.3f}, 90% CI [{l90:.3f}, {h90:.3f}], 95% CI [{l95:.3f}, "
192:               f"{h95:.3f}])", "L0", [str(BIN), str(TGT), SCRIPT], notes=f"prereg {regs[0]['id']}")
FILE .orchestra/LESSONS.md
1: # Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)
2: 
3: Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.
4: 
5: 1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
6:    predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
7: 2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
8:    volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
9: 3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
10:    that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
11: 4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
12:    to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
13: 5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
14:    input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
15: 6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
16:    (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
17: 7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
18:    carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
19: 8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
20:    so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
21:    (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
22: 9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
23:    ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
24:    multicomponent cells can be used.
25: 10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
26:     candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
27:     fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
28: 11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
29:     energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
30: 12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
31:     from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
32:     GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
33:     0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
34:     (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
35: 13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
36:     response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).
37: 
38: 14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
39:     at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
40:     gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
41:     which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
42:     Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
43:     design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.
44: 
45: 15. K' alone, fresh blind test (prereg 67a358fc59, result d92844787f, L2 entry recorded): 94 hm_fresh alloys, K' 4.22 ->
46:     1.89 GPa, gain 0.55, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08, 75/94 better. Two independent blind sets now agree for K' (k 1.08 both).
47:     K44 again weaker (gain 0.12, k 0.69, not gated). Why K44 transfers worse than K' is open: Co-rich outliers, or
48:     internal (non-affine) relaxation channels that the clamped protocol suppresses differently for the two shears.
49: 
50: 16. Model swap of the K' rule (prereg 851aec6883, result 86767e478d): medium-mpa-0, same geometry, same 94 hm_fresh
51:     alloys, binaries seed 0 only. K' 4.73 -> 2.28 GPa, gain 0.52, p 2.5e-4, but refit k 1.33 [1.11, 1.51]: the
52:     pre-registered k-contains-1 condition FAILS. K44 gain 0.16, k 0.77. Reading: that the alloy's K' follows the binaries
53:     at the alloy volume and cuts the error in half survives a model with a different shear bias; that the coefficient is
54:     exactly 1 does not (omat 1.08 twice, mpa 1.33). Binary seed noise would pull k down, not up. The two models disagree
55:     most at |dlnV| > 0.2 (K' corr 0.80 vs 0.96 within 0.1). Cause not yet audited. Do not claim "parameter-free" across
56:     models; the PBE check decides which k is physical.
57: 
58: 17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
59:     rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
60:     passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks
61:     K44" and "K44 needs a large signal" are not yet separated; match the two sets on |rule - pair| before claiming
62:     a Co mechanism (magnetism is a guess, MACE has no spin).
63:     Confound check (exploratory, same fresh rows, tertiles of |rule - pair|): at matched signal Co-free gain 0.37 / 0.58
64:     vs Co 0.08 / 0.22 (mid / large), and Co alloys carry a larger floor at small signal (rule rms 2.61 vs 1.73 GPa).
65:     The Co effect survives signal matching; not yet a registered claim.
66: 
67: 18. Why K44 looked broken (Opus, swarm S2, blind by file timestamp, confirmed on 60 Co alloys). The part the pair rule
68:     misses is the same in both shears (corr 0.71, slope ~1). K44's volume signal is half of K''s, so the shared floor
69:     swamps it; in Co alloys the floor anticorrelates with the signal and drags k to 0.7. Remove the floor (A = K44 - K'
70:     or e' as covariate) and K44 transfers with k ~1. LESSONS 14-16 failure reason: design, not hypothesis.
71: 
72: 19. Shared SQS seed leak (Opus S2 audit, Astra confirmed). compute.py:56 draws the site permutation from (seed, n)
73:     only, so every seed-0 cell thresholds one random field: seed-0 targets and seed-0 binaries share configuration
74:     noise. K' is immune (gain 0.55-0.58, k 1.07-1.10 for every seed split). K44 is not: leak-free gain 0.06-0.14,
75:     k 0.60-0.77. d9460850ce and the LESSONS 18 Co check used the leak; 9cfc8edaf0 was withdrawn before reading and
76:     re-registered as c2eff007ad with target seed 100. Rule: targets and inputs never share a seed.
77: 
78: 20. Shared floor, disjoint seeds (c2eff007ad -> b86e0d8a40 PASS, 150 alloys): A = K44 - K' transfers (gain 0.49),
79:     corr(e44, e') 0.77, joint k 0.91, b 0.94; plain K44 Co-free gain 0.47, Co 0.09. Astra audit: PLAUSIBLE, the
80:     null could not separate a compositional floor from same-cell noise. A shared-channel claim needs targets for the
81:     two channels from different cells. Test fd786169e3.
82: 
83: 21. The shared floor is compositional (fd786169e3 PASS, two cells per composition, unique seeds): cross-cell corr
84:     0.75 vs same-cell 0.79, k 0.92, b 0.95; Astra audit PLAUSIBLE (cell noise ~5% of the shared covariance). Next
85:     doubt is a known identity: clamped curvatures carry the initial stress, K44 = C44 + s_yy, K' = C' + (s_xx+s_yy)/2.
86:     A floor claim must survive subtracting it (k_floor_stress.py). Pre-register every step; one audit, one test.
87: 
88: 22. The floor survives the known pre-stress identity (ede47f1d65 PASS; Astra PLAUSIBLE): corrected cross-cell r
89:     0.67, k 0.99, b 0.79. Mixing pre-stress is 7 GPa rms but pair-additive (rule leaves 0.7 GPa), so it was never the
90:     floor. Remaining doubt: error shared through the binary references (b drops to 0.4-0.5 with single disjoint
91:     seeds). Shared-residual claims need two independent binary panels, as in k_mpa_equiv.py.

FILE harness/context.py
1: """What a candidate formula may use: per-element and per-binary inputs, never the alloy's own target.
2: 
3: ctx.pure[el]      dict: V (A^3/atom, MACE fcc), B, G, C11, C12, C44 (GPa), r, chi, vec, tm
4: ctx.pair[(a, b)]  dict for sorted element pairs, 50:50 random clamped binary at its Vegard volume V_ij:
5:                   E (eV/atom), D = dE/dlnV, D2 = d2E/dlnV2 (eV/atom), V (A^3/atom); mean over SQS seeds 0-2
6: ctx.vegard(comp)  Vegard volume of a composition
7: ctx.pairs(comp)   iterator over (a, b, x_a, x_b) for unlike pairs
8: """
9: 
10: from __future__ import annotations
11: 
12: from functools import lru_cache
13: from itertools import combinations
14: from pathlib import Path
15: 
16: import pandas as pd
17: 
18: from harness.features import elem, parse_comp
19: 
20: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
21: 
22: 
23: class Context:
24:     def __init__(self):
25:         p = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv").set_index("el")
26:         self.pure = {}
27:         for el, r in p.iterrows():
28:             self.pure[el] = {"V": r.vol_per_atom, "B": r.B, "G": r.G, "C11": r.C11, "C12": r.C12, "C44": r.C44,
29:                              **elem(el)}
30:         h1 = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "h1_ev_rows.csv")
31:         h1["c"] = h1.comp.map(parse_comp)
32:         eq = h1[(h1.n_el == 2) & h1.c.map(lambda c: all(abs(v - 0.5) < 1e-3 for v in c.values()))]
33:         rows = [eq[["comp", "E_mix", "dE_dlnV", "d2E_dlnV2"]]]
34:         seeds = ROOT / "data" / "binary_seeds.csv"
35:         if seeds.exists():
36:             rows.append(pd.read_csv(seeds)[["comp", "E_mix", "dE_dlnV", "d2E_dlnV2"]])
37:         b = pd.concat(rows)
38:         b["pair"] = b.comp.map(lambda s: tuple(sorted(parse_comp(s))))
39:         m = b.groupby("pair")[["E_mix", "dE_dlnV", "d2E_dlnV2"]].mean()
40:         self.pair = {k: {"E": r.E_mix, "D": r.dE_dlnV, "D2": r.d2E_dlnV2,
41:                          "V": 0.5 * (self.pure[k[0]]["V"] + self.pure[k[1]]["V"])} for k, r in m.iterrows()}
42: 
43:     def vegard(self, comp: dict) -> float:
44:         return sum(x * self.pure[e]["V"] for e, x in comp.items())
45: 
46:     def pairs(self, comp: dict):
47:         for a, b in combinations(sorted(comp), 2):
48:             yield a, b, comp[a], comp[b]
49: 
50: 
51: @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
52: def context() -> Context:
53:     return Context()
FILE harness/compute.py
1: """Structure generation, relaxation and elastic constants with a universal ML potential."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import datetime as dt
6: import os
7: import time
8: from functools import lru_cache
9: 
10: import numpy as np
11: from ase import Atoms
12: from ase.build import bulk
13: from ase.filters import FrechetCellFilter
14: from ase.optimize import FIRE
15: 
16: from harness.reference import ELASTIC_EXP
17: 
18: GPA = 160.21766208  # eV/A^3 -> GPa
19: MODEL = os.environ.get("HARNESS_MODEL", "medium-omat-0")  # mace_mp foundation model name
20: 
21: # Rough lattice parameters (A) for the starting guess only; relaxation sets the real value.
22: A0 = {"fcc": {"Al": 4.05, "Cu": 3.61, "Ni": 3.52, "Ag": 4.09, "Au": 4.08, "Pd": 3.89,
23:               "Pt": 3.92, "Co": 3.54, "Fe": 3.59, "Cr": 3.60, "Mn": 3.60},
24:       "bcc": {"Fe": 2.87, "Cr": 2.88, "Mo": 3.15, "W": 3.16, "V": 3.03, "Nb": 3.30,
25:               "Ta": 3.30, "Ti": 3.28, "Zr": 3.57, "Hf": 3.50, "Al": 3.24}}
26: 
27: 
28: @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
29: def calculator():
30:     from mace.calculators import mace_mp
31:     import torch
32:     device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
33:     return mace_mp(model=MODEL, device=device, default_dtype="float64")
34: 
35: 
36: def site_counts(comp: dict[str, float], n: int) -> dict[str, int]:
37:     counts = {el: int(round(x * n)) for el, x in comp.items()}
38:     counts[max(counts, key=counts.get)] += n - sum(counts.values())
39:     return counts
40: 
41: 
42: def actual_fractions(atoms: Atoms) -> dict[str, float]:
43:     """Composition the cell really has. Subtract pure references with these, not the nominal fractions (the
44:     rounding to whole atoms shifted E_mix by up to ~57 meV/atom before 2026-10-31)."""
45:     s = atoms.get_chemical_symbols()
46:     return {el: s.count(el) / len(s) for el in sorted(set(s))}
47: 
48: 
49: def solid_solution(comp: dict[str, float], lattice: str, reps: int, seed: int) -> Atoms:
50:     """Random solid solution on a cubic conventional supercell (no SQS optimisation). Counts are rounded to whole
51:     atoms; use actual_fractions() for references."""
52:     a = sum(x * A0[lattice].get(el, 3.5 if lattice == "fcc" else 3.1) for el, x in comp.items())
53:     atoms = bulk("X", lattice, a=a, cubic=True).repeat((reps, reps, reps))
54:     counts = site_counts(comp, len(atoms))
55:     symbols = [el for el, c in counts.items() for _ in range(c)]
56:     np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle(symbols)
57:     atoms.set_chemical_symbols(symbols)
58:     return atoms
59: 
60: 
61: # GPU duty cycle in (0, 1]: after each relaxation sleep so the GPU is busy only this fraction
62: # of the time. Keeps a laptop from overheating on long scans; results are unaffected.
63: DUTY = float(os.environ.get("HARNESS_DUTY", "1.0"))
64: 
65: 
66: def relax(atoms: Atoms, cell: bool, fmax: float = 1e-3, steps: int = 400) -> int:
67:     atoms.calc = calculator()
68:     target = FrechetCellFilter(atoms) if cell else atoms
69:     opt = FIRE(target, logfile=None)
70:     t = time.perf_counter()
71:     opt.run(fmax=fmax, steps=steps)
72:     if DUTY < 1:
73:         time.sleep((time.perf_counter() - t) * (1 / DUTY - 1))
74:     return opt.nsteps
75: 
76: 
77: def elastic_tensor(atoms: Atoms, eps: float = 0.005, relax_ions: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
78:     """Full 6x6 Voigt tensor (GPa) from central differences of stress, ions relaxed at each strain."""
79:     cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
80:     C = np.zeros((6, 6))
81:     voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]
82:     for j, (k, l) in enumerate(voigt):
83:         sig = []
84:         for s in (+eps, -eps):
85:             e = np.zeros((3, 3))
86:             if k == l:
87:                 e[k, k] = s
88:             else:
89:                 e[k, l] = e[l, k] = s / 2  # engineering shear strain = s
90:             strained = atoms.copy()
91:             strained.set_cell(cell0 @ (np.eye(3) + e), scale_atoms=True)
92:             strained.calc = calculator()
93:             if relax_ions and len(strained) > 1:
94:                 relax(strained, cell=False, fmax=5e-4)
95:             sig.append(strained.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA)  # ASE: tensile stress positive
96:         C[:, j] = (sig[0] - sig[1]) / (2 * eps)
97:     return 0.5 * (C + C.T)
98: 
99: 
100: def cubic_average(C: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
101:     """Project a (noisy, random alloy) 6x6 tensor onto cubic symmetry."""
102:     c11 = np.mean([C[0, 0], C[1, 1], C[2, 2]])
103:     c12 = np.mean([C[0, 1], C[0, 2], C[1, 2]])
104:     c44 = np.mean([C[3, 3], C[4, 4], C[5, 5]])
105:     return float(c11), float(c12), float(c44)
106: 
107: 
108: def voigt_reuss_hill(c11: float, c12: float, c44: float) -> dict[str, float]:
109:     B = (c11 + 2 * c12) / 3
110:     Gv = (c11 - c12 + 3 * c44) / 5
111:     Gr = 5 * (c11 - c12) * c44 / (4 * c44 + 3 * (c11 - c12))
112:     G = (Gv + Gr) / 2
113:     E = 9 * B * G / (3 * B + G)
114:     nu = (3 * B - 2 * G) / (2 * (3 * B + G))
115:     return {"B": B, "G": G, "E": E, "nu": nu, "pugh": B / G, "cauchy": c12 - c44,
116:             "zener": 2 * c44 / (c11 - c12)}
117: 
118: 
119: def run_alloy(comp: dict[str, float], lattice: str, reps: int = 3, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
120:     atoms = solid_solution(comp, lattice, reps, seed)
121:     nsteps = relax(atoms, cell=True)
122:     C = elastic_tensor(atoms)
123:     c11, c12, c44 = cubic_average(C)
124:     # Quality flag: spread of the three cubic-equivalent C11 and C44 entries. Large spread means the
125:     # random cell is too small for its chemistry or the solid solution broke symmetry on relaxing.
126:     spread = float(max(np.ptp(np.diag(C)[:3]) / c11, np.ptp(np.diag(C)[3:]) / max(c44, 1.0)))
127:     vol = atoms.get_volume() / len(atoms)
128:     row = {"formula": atoms.get_chemical_formula(mode="metal"),
129:            "comp": ";".join(f"{el}:{x:.4f}" for el, x in sorted(comp.items())),
130:            "lattice": lattice, "natoms": len(atoms), "seed": seed, "model": MODEL,
131:            "vol_per_atom": vol, "a_eff": (vol * (4 if lattice == "fcc" else 2)) ** (1 / 3),
132:            "relax_steps": nsteps, "cubic_spread": spread, "C11": c11, "C12": c12, "C44": c44,
133:            "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
134:     row.update(voigt_reuss_hill(c11, c12, c44))
135:     return row
136: 
137: 
138: def calibrate(elements: list[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
139:     rows = []
140:     for el in elements or list(ELASTIC_EXP):
141:         lattice, e11, e12, e44 = ELASTIC_EXP[el]
142:         r = run_alloy({el: 1.0}, lattice, reps=1)
143:         r["el"] = el
144:         r.update({"C11_exp": e11, "C12_exp": e12, "C44_exp": e44})
145:         r.update({f"{k}_exp": v for k, v in voigt_reuss_hill(e11, e12, e44).items()})
146:         rows.append(r)
147:     return rows
FILE scripts/k_shear_transfer.py
1: """Shear-curvature volume transfer (swarm S1, open front, Opus): a new observable for the champion's mechanism.
2: 
3: python scripts/k_shear_transfer.py
4: Claim: the clamped mixing shear curvatures of random fcc alloys are pair sums of 50:50 binary curvatures taken at the
5: alloy's own volume, K_alloy(V0) = sum 4 x_i x_j K_ij(V0), with no parameter. Baseline: the same pair sum at each
6: binary's own Vegard volume V_ij.
7: Order, so that the test is blind:
8:  1. binaries: K44, K' of the 50:50 binaries (SQS seeds 0-2) on a ln(V/V_ij) grid -> data/binary_kgrid.csv
9:  2. predictions on the h3_fresh compositions (comp_actual, n_el >= 3; K never computed there), power by simulation,
10:     pre-registration in the ledger
11:  3. targets: the same a2 protocol on those alloys, references at the cell's actual fractions -> data/h3_shear_clamped.csv
12:  4. test: per channel RMSE(rule) <= 0.9 RMSE(pair at V_ij) and paired sign-flip p < 0.005 (two channels); PASS needs
13:     both channels. Secondary (reported, not gated): Opus's prior on median dlnK/dlnV of binaries with |K| > 10 GPa,
14:     K44 in [-5, -1.5], K' in [-6, -2].
15: """
16: 
17: import datetime as dt
18: import os
19: import sys
20: import time
21: from pathlib import Path
22: 
23: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
24: os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
25: sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
26: 
27: import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
28: import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
29: from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402
30: from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline  # noqa: E402
31:

33: from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402

35: from harness.features import parse_comp  # noqa: E402

37: AMPS = np.array([-0.01, -0.005, 0.0, 0.005, 0.01])
38: GRID = [-0.40, -0.30, -0.20, -0.15, -0.10, -0.05, 0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40]
39: BIN, TGT = ROOT / "data" / "binary_kgrid.csv", ROOT / "data" / "h3_shear_clamped.csv"
40: ctx = context()
41: calc = compute.calculator()

44: 
45: def e_strained(atoms, v_atom, F):
46:     a = atoms.copy()
47:     a.set_cell(a.cell * (v_atom * len(a) / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
48:     a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
49:     a.calc = calc
50:     t = time.perf_counter()
51:     e = a.get_potential_energy() / len(a)
52:     time.sleep(time.perf_counter() - t)  # 50% duty cycle, keeps the laptop cool
53:     return e

55: 
56: def F_of(name, s):
57:     if name == "K44":
58:         F = np.eye(3)
59:         F[0, 1] = s
60:         return F
61:     return np.diag([np.exp(s), np.exp(-s), 1.0])

63: 
64: def curvatures(alloy, x, v):

1: """Structure generation, relaxation and elastic constants with a universal ML potential."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import datetime as dt
6: import os
7: import time
8: from functools import lru_cache
9: 
10: import numpy as np
11: from ase import Atoms
12: from ase.build import bulk
13: from ase.filters import FrechetCellFilter
14: from ase.optimize import FIRE
15: 
16: from harness.reference import ELASTIC_EXP
17: 
18: GPA = 160.21766208  # eV/A^3 -> GPa
19: MODEL = os.environ.get("HARNESS_MODEL", "medium-omat-0")  # mace_mp foundation model name
20: 
21: # Rough lattice parameters (A) for the starting guess only; relaxation sets the real value.
22: A0 = {"fcc": {"Al": 4.05, "Cu": 3.61, "Ni": 3.52, "Ag": 4.09, "Au": 4.08, "Pd": 3.89,
23:               "Pt": 3.92, "Co": 3.54, "Fe": 3.59, "Cr": 3.60, "Mn": 3.60},
24:       "bcc": {"Fe": 2.87, "Cr": 2.88, "Mo": 3.15, "W": 3.16, "V": 3.03, "Nb": 3.30,
25:               "Ta": 3.30, "Ti": 3.28, "Zr": 3.57, "Hf": 3.50, "Al": 3.24}}
26: 
27: 
28: @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
29: def calculator():
30:     from mace.calculators import mace_mp
31:     import torch
32:     device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
33:     return mace_mp(model=MODEL, device=device, default_dtype="float64")
34: 
35: 
36: def site_counts(comp: dict[str, float], n: int) -> dict[str, int]:
37:     counts = {el: int(round(x * n)) for el, x in comp.items()}
38:     counts[max(counts, key=counts.get)] += n - sum(counts.values())
39:     return counts
40: 
41: 
42: def actual_fractions(atoms: Atoms) -> dict[str, float]:
43:     """Composition the cell really has. Subtract pure references with these, not the nominal fractions (the
44:     rounding to whole atoms shifted E_mix by up to ~57 meV/atom before 2026-10-31)."""
45:     s = atoms.get_chemical_symbols()
46:     return {el: s.count(el) / len(s) for el in sorted(set(s))}
47: 
48: 
49: def solid_solution(comp: dict[str, float], lattice: str, reps: int, seed: int) -> Atoms:
50:     """Random solid solution on a cubic conventional supercell (no SQS optimisation). Counts are rounded to whole
51:     atoms; use actual_fractions() for references."""
52:     a = sum(x * A0[lattice].get(el, 3.5 if lattice == "fcc" else 3.1) for el, x in comp.items())
53:     atoms = bulk("X", lattice, a=a, cubic=True).repeat((reps, reps, reps))
54:     counts = site_counts(comp, len(atoms))
55:     symbols = [el for el, c in counts.items() for _ in range(c)]
56:     np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle(symbols)
57:     atoms.set_chemical_symbols(symbols)
58:     return atoms
59: 
60: 
61: # GPU duty cycle in (0, 1]: after each relaxation sleep so the GPU is busy only this fraction
62: # of the time. Keeps a laptop from overheating on long scans; results are unaffected.
63: DUTY = float(os.environ.get("HARNESS_DUTY", "1.0"))
64: 
65: 
66: def relax(atoms: Atoms, cell: bool, fmax: float = 1e-3, steps: int = 400) -> int:
67:     atoms.calc = calculator()
68:     target = FrechetCellFilter(atoms) if cell else atoms
69:     opt = FIRE(target, logfile=None)
70:     t = time.perf_counter()
71:     opt.run(fmax=fmax, steps=steps)

"""Is the shared shear floor a property of the composition or of the cell? (audit of b86e0d8a40, Astra)

python scripts/k_floor_cells.py
b86e0d8a40 passed, but K44 and K' came from the same seed-100 cell, so a residual shared by the two channels can be
single-cell configuration noise. Here every composition of that test gets two new cells with seeds unique to that
cell (2000 + 2i, 2001 + 2i), so no two cells share a permutation field and none shares one with the binaries (0-2).
A composition-level floor shows up across cells; cell noise does not.
PASS needs both: (1) cross-cell corr(e44 of cell a, e' of cell b), averaged over (a,b) and (b,a), >= 0.5; (2) the
joint fit K44_a - pair44 = k T44 + b e'_b, pooled over both orders, gives k in [0.7, 1.3] and b in [0.6, 1.3].
"""

import datetime as dt
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import importlib.util  # noqa: E402

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402

from harness import ledger  # noqa: E402

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("kst", ROOT / "scripts" / "k_shear_transfer.py")
kst = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(kst)
from harness import compute  # noqa: E402
from harness.features import parse_comp  # noqa: E402

ctx, curvatures = kst.ctx, kst.curvatures
spl = kst.spl
SRC = ROOT / "data" / "k_aniso_s100_clamped.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "data" / "k_floor_cells.csv"
SCRIPT = str(Path(__file__))
CLAIM = "Shared shear floor is compositional"

comps = list(pd.read_csv(SRC).comp)


def pr(c, ch, at):
    v = ctx.vegard(c)
    return sum(4 * xa * xb * float(spl[((a, b), ch)](np.log(v / ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]) if at else 0.0))
               for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))


C = [parse_comp(s) for s in comps]
R44, P44, RP = (np.array([pr(c, "K44", 1) for c in C]), np.array([pr(c, "K44", 0) for c in C]),
                np.array([pr(c, "Kp", 1) for c in C]))
T44 = R44 - P44


def judge(y44a, ypa, y44b, ypb):
    e44a, epa, e44b, epb = y44a - R44, ypa - RP, y44b - R44, ypb - RP
    r = 0.5 * (np.corrcoef(e44a, epb)[0, 1] + np.corrcoef(e44b, epa)[0, 1])
    X = np.r_[np.c_[T44, epb], np.c_[T44, epa]]
    Y = np.r_[y44a - P44, y44b - P44]
    k, b = np.linalg.lstsq(X, Y, rcond=None)[0]
    return bool(r >= 0.5 and 0.7 <= k <= 1.3 and 0.6 <= b <= 1.3), float(r), float(k), float(b)


# Power. H: a composition floor F (sd 2.4) shared by both channels, channel-specific composition terms (sd 0.8) and
# independent cell noise of the measured size (K44 1.44, K' 0.79 GPa; S2 audit). Null: no shared composition term;
# the same-cell correlation (~0.75, as observed) comes from cell noise u (sd 2.2) shared by the two channels of a cell.
regs = [e for e in ledger.entries() if e["claim"].startswith(CLAIM) and "prereg" in e["notes"]]
if not regs:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
    n = len(C)

    def draw(h):
        if h:
            F, g44, gp = rng.normal(0, 2.4, n), rng.normal(0, 0.8, n), rng.normal(0, 0.8, n)
            cell = lambda: (rng.normal(0, 1.44, n), rng.normal(0, 0.79, n))  # noqa: E731
        else:
            F, g44, gp = np.zeros(n), rng.normal(0, 1.0, n), rng.normal(0, 1.0, n)

            def cell():
                u = rng.normal(0, 2.2, n)
                return u + rng.normal(0, 0.6, n), u + rng.normal(0, 0.4, n)
        out = []
        for _ in range(2):
            n44, np_ = cell()
            out += [R44 + F + g44 + n44, RP + F + gp + np_]
        return out

const fs=require('fs'),crypto=require('crypto');
function csv(f){let z=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').trim().split(/\\r?\\n/),h=z.shift().split(',');return z.map(l=>Object.fromEntries(l.split(',').map((v,i)=>[h[i],v"'!=='"''&&Number.isFinite(+v)?+v:v])));}
const mean=a=>a.reduce((s,x)=>s+x,0)/a.length, sum=a=>a.reduce((s,x)=>s+x,0), rm=a=>Math.sqrt(mean(a.map(x=>x*x)));
function solve(A,b){A=A.map((r,i)=>[...r,b[i]]);let n=b.length;for(let j=0;j<n;j++){let p=j;for(let i=j+1;i<n;i++)if(Math.abs(A[i][j])>Math.abs(A[p][j]))p=i;[A[j],A[p]]=[A[p],A[j]];let v=A[j][j];for(let k=j;k<=n;k++)A[j][k]/=v;for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(i"'!==j){let v=A[i][j];for(let k=j;k<=n;k++)A[i][k]-=v*A[j][k];}}return A.map(r=>r[n]);}
function spline(x,y,linear=false){let n=x.length,h=x.slice(1).map((v,i)=>v-x[i]),A=Array.from({length:n},()=>Array(n).fill(0)),b=Array(n).fill(0);
A[0][0]=-h[1];A[0][1]=h[0]+h[1];A[0][2]=-h[0];A[n-1][n-3]=-h[n-2];A[n-1][n-2]=h[n-3]+h[n-2];A[n-1][n-1]=-h[n-3];
for(let i=1;i<n-1;i++){A[i][i-1]=h[i-1];A[i][i]=2*(h[i-1]+h[i]);A[i][i+1]=h[i];b[i]=6*((y[i+1]-y[i])/h[i]-(y[i]-y[i-1])/h[i-1]);}let M=solve(A,b);
return t=>{let i=0;while(i<n-2&&t>x[i+1])i++;let a=(x[i+1]-t)/h[i],c=(t-x[i])/h[i];return a*y[i]+c*y[i+1]+(linear?0:((a*a*a-a)*M[i]+(c*c*c-c)*M[i+1])*h[i]*h[i]/6);};}
const pure=Object.fromEntries(csv('"'data/scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv').map(r=>[r.el,r.vol_per_atom]));
function comp(s,exact=true){return Object.fromEntries(s.split(';').map(t=>{let[e,x]=t.split(':');return[e,exact?Math.round(+x*108)/108:+x]}));}
function curveTable(f,linear=false){let groups={};for(let r of csv(f)){let key=r.seed+':'+r.pair;(groups[key]??=[]).push(r);}return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(groups).map(([k,g])=>{g.sort((a,b)=>a.dlnV-b.dlnV);return[k,spline(g.map(r=>r.dlnV),g.map(r=>r.Kp),linear)]}));}
function terms(c,V=pure){let els=Object.keys(c).sort(),v=sum(els.map(e=>c[e]*V[e])),ts=[];for(let i=0;i<els.length;i++)for(let j=i+1;j<els.length;j++){let a=els[i],b=els[j],p=a+'-'+b;ts.push({p,w:4*c[a]*c[b],d:Math.log(v/(.5*(pure[a]+pure[b])))});}return ts;}
function preds(rows,table,seeds,exact=true,V=pure){return seeds.map(seed=>rows.map(r=>{let ts=terms(comp(r.comp,exact),V);return {r:sum(ts.map(t=>t.w*table[seed+':'+t.p](t.d))),p:sum(ts.map(t=>t.w*table[seed+':'+t.p](0))),ts};}));}
function avgPred(pp,ss=pp.map((_,i)=>i)){return pp[0].map((_,i)=>({r:mean(ss.map(j=>pp[j][i].r)),p:mean(ss.map(j=>pp[j][i].p))}));}

function preds(rows,table,seeds,exact=true,V=pure){return seeds.map(seed=>rows.map(r=>{let ts=terms(comp(r.comp,exact),V);return {r:sum(ts.map(t=>t.w*table[seed+':'+t.p](t.d))),p:sum(ts.map(t=>t.w*table[seed+':'+t.p](0))),ts};}));}
function avgPred(pp,ss=pp.map((_,i)=>i)){return pp[0].map((_,i)=>({r:mean(ss.map(j=>pp[j][i].r)),p:mean(ss.map(j=>pp[j][i].p))}));}
function stat(rows,A,B,idx=rows.map((_,i)=>i)){let ns=idx.map(i=>{let y=rows[i].Kp,a=A[i],b=B[i],ta=a.r-a.p,tb=b.r-b.p;return (ta*(y-b.p)+tb*(y-a.p))/2}),ds=idx.map(i=>(A[i].r-A[i].p)*(B[i].r-B[i].p)), k=sum(ns)/sum(ds);let er=idx.map(i=>rows[i].Kp-(A[i].r+B[i].r)/2),ep=idx.map(i=>rows[i].Kp-(A[i].p+B[i].p)/2),ef=idx.map(i=>ep[idx.indexOf(i)]-k*((A[i].r+B[i].r-A[i].p-B[i].p)/2));
return {n:idx.length,k,den:sum(ds),pair:rm(ep),rule:rm(er),gain:1-rm(er)/rm(ep),fit:rm(ef),better:sum(er.map((e,j)=>Math.abs(e)<Math.abs(ep[j])?1:0))};}
function groupTargets(f){let g={};for(let r of csv(f))(g[r.comp]??=[]).push(r);return Object.values(g).map(rs=>({...rs[0],Kp:mean(rs.map(r=>r.Kp)),cells:rs}));}
function rng(seed=1){let a=seed|0;return()=>{a|=0;a=a+0x6D2B79F5|0;let t=Math.imul(a"'^a>>>15,1|a);t=t+Math.imul(t''^t>>>7,61|t)''^t;return((t''^t>>>14)>>>0)/4294967296;};}
function quant(a,p){a=[...a].sort((x,y)=>x-y);let j=(a.length-1)*p,i=Math.floor(j);return a[i]+(j-i)*(a[Math.min(i+1,a.length-1)]-a[i]);}
function boot(rows,ppA,ppB,n=10000,s=44,bin=true,compBoot=true){let rand=rng(s),out=[];for(let b=0;b<n;b++){let sa=ppA.map((_,i)=>bin?Math.floor(rand()*ppA.length):i),sb=ppB.map((_,i)=>bin?Math.floor(rand()*ppB.length):i);let num=0,den=0;for(let j=0;j<rows.length;j++){let i=compBoot?Math.floor(rand()*rows.length):j,aR=mean(sa.map(k=>ppA[k][i].r)),aP=mean(sa.map(k=>ppA[k][i].p)),bR=mean(sb.map(k=>ppB[k][i].r)),bP=mean(sb.map(k=>ppB[k][i].p));let ta=aR-aP,tb=bR-bP;num+=(ta*(rows[i].Kp-bP)+tb*(rows[i].Kp-aP))/2;den+=ta*tb;}out.push(num/den);}return{ci90:[quant(out,.05),quant(out,.95)],ci95:[quant(out,.025),quant(out,.975)],sd:Math.sqrt(mean(out.map(x=>(x-mean(out))**2)))};}

**VERDICT: hypothesis.** Kayıtlı kompozisyon dağılımı ve hacim tanımı altında toplu katsayı gerçekten **k ≈ 1,138**; FAIL’i açıklayan bir hesaplama hatası bulmadım. Ancak **1,14 evrensel bir katsayı değil**: sapma kompozisyona güçlü biçimde bağlı. Ayrıca eşdeğerlik testinin başarısızlığı, **k > 1,10’un kesinleştiği** anlamına gelmiyor; güven aralığı 1,10’u hâlâ içeriyor.

Dosyaları değiştirmedim. Aşağıdaki sayıları CSV’lerden bağımsız JavaScript hesabıyla yeniden ürettim.

1. **Kayıt, veri ve sonuç birbiriyle uyuşuyor.** [claims.jsonl:84](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/claims/claims.jsonl:84>), [k_mpa_equiv.py:184](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:184>).

   Kodun ve iki CSV’nin SHA256 önekleri defterle eşleşiyor. **1.200 benzersiz kompozisyon × iki hücre**, ayrıca **2.808 benzersiz ikili/seed/hacim kaydı** var. Yeniden hesap:
   
   - **k = 1,1382727**
   - 10.000 bootstrap: **%90 CI [1,0979; 1,1816]**, **%95 CI [1,0898; 1,1897]**
   - Sabit altı tabakayı koruyan bootstrap: **%95 CI [1,0916; 1,1898]**

   Dolayısıyla kayıtlı FAIL doğru; tam **k=1** de bu belirsizlik hesabında dışlanıyor.

2. **`predict`, `khat`, indeksleme ve oranlar FAIL’in nedeni değil.** [k_mpa_equiv.py:94](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:94>), [compute.py:36](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/harness/compute.py:36>).

   `TI` kompozisyon, `TP` sıralı çift indeksidir; `bincount` üçüncü argümanı doğru biçimde `minlength` olarak kullanılıyor. Çift sırası, grid sırası ve çapraz panel formülü doğru. Üretimde oranlar tam **atom sayısı/108**, saf referanslar gerçek hücre oranlarıdır. CSV’deki dört basamaklı oranları doğrudan kullanmak k’yi yalnız **+0,000053** değiştiriyor.

   Altı seed’in bütün benzersiz 3+3 panel bölünmelerinde k **1,13803–1,13851**. Yalnız ikili bootstrap belirsizliği **SE≈0,00168**; toplam **SE≈0,02536**. Üçer seed sınırlı olsa da mevcut panel oynaklığı **+0,138** sapmayı açıklamıyor.

3. **Sapma bütün tabakalara yayılmış değil; özellikle Cu içeren sistemlerde.** [k_mpa_equiv.py:89](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:89>), [k_mpa_equiv_targets.csv:2](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/data/k_mpa_equiv_targets.csv:2>).

   | Alt küme | n | Çapraz k | Bootstrap %95 CI |
   |---|---:|---:|---:|
   | 3 element | 400 | **0,997** | [0,914; 1,086] |
   | 4 element | 400 | **1,248** | [1,177; 1,331] |
   | 5 element | 400 | **1,173** | [1,112; 1,238] |
   | Cu yok | 670 | **0,999** | [0,938; 1,069] |
   | Cu var | 530 | **1,235** | [1,174; 1,299] |

   Co’suz/Co’lu toplamlar **1,1368/1,1390** olsa da bu eşitlik alt yapıdaki farkları gizliyor. Co–Cu içeren 241 kompozisyon çıkarılınca k **1,055**; Cu–Ir içerenler çıkarılınca **1,127** oluyor. Buna karşılık en yüksek regresyon ağırlıklı %1 çıkarıldığında k **1,195’e yükseliyor**: birkaç uç satırın yarattığı bir sapma değil.

   Bunlar **keşifsel duyarlılık analizleri**; çift çıkarmak kompozisyon dağılımını da değiştirir, dolayısıyla nedensel çift ataması değildir.

4. **Grid dışına taşma yok; hacim aralığı etkili ama tek açıklama değil.** [k_mpa_equiv.py:35](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:35>), [k_mpa_equiv.py:105](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:105>).

   **7.600 çift sorgusunun tamamı** grid içinde: `dlnV ∈ [−0,31690; +0,37106]`, grid ±0,40. Her kompozisyondaki en büyük `|dlnV|` üzerinden:

   - ≤0,15: **n=472, k=1,066**
   - ≤0,25: **n=1.069, k=1,114**
   - >0,25: **n=131, k=1,411**

   Büyük hacim farkları sapmayı artırıyor, fakat onları çıkarmak k’yi 1’e indirmiyor. Cubic yerine linear interpolation **k=1,164** veriyor; FAIL kurtulmuyor. Ham strain enerjileri ve daha sık hacim örnekleri bulunmadığından sonlu-gerinim/grid yakınsamasını tamamen doğrulanmış saymıyorum.

5. **Omat geometrisi tutarlı kullanılmış; yukarı yönlü bir geometri hatası gösterilemiyor.** [context.py:25](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/harness/context.py:25>), [k_mpa_equiv.py:161](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:161>), [k_mpa_equiv.py:174](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:174>).

   İkili eğrisi fiziksel olarak `V_ij^omat × exp(dlnV)` hacminde hesaplanıyor; `ln(V0^omat/V_ij^omat)` sorgusu onu **hedefin hesaplandığı aynı V0’ya** getiriyor. Yanlış hacim eşleştirmesi yok.

   Bununla birlikte ölçülen özellik **mpa’nın kendi denge geometrisindeki özellik değil**, omat hacminde clamped eğrilik. Mevcut saf-element sonuçlarında mpa hacim farkı Cu’da **+%0,54**, Pt’de **+%1,24**. Hedefleri yeni hacimde hesaplamadan bunun k üzerindeki yönü/büyüklüğü belirlenemez. Yalnız `V_ij` tabanını değiştirmek de katsayının tanımını değiştirir; sabit hedef hacmindeki parametresiz tahmini değiştirmez.

6. **Hacim transferinin büyük tahmin kazancı sağlaması ayakta.** [k_mpa_equiv.py:99](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:99>).

   İki panel ortalamasıyla:

   | Tahmin | RMSE |
   |---|---:|
   | Pair-at-`V_ij` | **4,8118 GPa** |
   | Hacim transferi, k=1 | **2,2130 GPa** |
   | Aynı veride k=1,138 fit’i | **2,1505 GPa** |

   Parametresiz kural **%54,0 RMSE azalması** sağlıyor ve **934/1.200** kompozisyonda daha iyi. Katsayı fit’inin ek kazancı yalnız **%2,8**; ayrıca bu son sayı eğitim içi, bağımsız doğrulama değil.

7. **Omat’ın aynı hassasiyette k=1’i dışlaması mümkün; mevcut kontrol zaten buna işaret ediyor.** [k_floor_cells.py:103](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_floor_cells.py:103>), [k_floor_cells.csv:2](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/data/k_floor_cells.csv:2>).

   Eski h3/hm katsayılarını **1,08195/1,07855** olarak yeniden buldum. Daha güçlü kontrol olan 150 kompozisyon × iki bağımsız omat hedef hücresinde, mevcut ikilileri seed **0 | 1,2** olarak ayırınca **k=1,1065**, koşullu bootstrap **%95 CI≈[1,019;1,201]**. Diğer iki panel bölünmesinde de aralık 1’i dışlıyor. Omat’ta 3/4/5 element katsayıları **1,007/1,187/1,165**: mpa’daki tabakalaşmaya benziyor.

   **Bu, aynı 1.200 kompozisyon ve 3+3 seed tasarımı değildir**; tek-seed panelin belirsizliği bootstrap ile tam öğrenilemez. Dolayısıyla “omat kesin geçerdi” de “mpa–omat farkı kanıtlandı” da denemez. Eski PASS kapıları zaten esas olarak tahmin kazancını sınamıştı.

8. **Güç simülasyonu iyimserdi; yine de bu FAIL’i `design` yapmıyor.** [k_mpa_equiv.py:130](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:130>).

   Simülasyon iki hücreyle hedef saçılımını **2,36/√2=1,67 GPa** kabul ediyor. Ölçülen iki-hücre ortalamasının kural artığı **2,21 GPa**; tek-hücre rastgele saçılımı ise yalnız **0,682 GPa**. Kompozisyona bağlı artık hücre ortalamasıyla kaybolmuyor. Bildirilen `%100 power` bu nedenle fazla kesin. Buna rağmen gerçek veriden hesaplanan aralık yeterince dar ve 1’den uzak: burada sonuç yalnız düşük güç yüzünden belirsiz kalmış değil.

**Desteklenen iddia:** İki seçenek arasında **“yaklaşık 1,1 civarında etkin katsayılı hacim transferi”** daha doğru. Fakat “model-dependent” henüz ayrıştırılmış değil; **kompozisyon dağılımına bağımlılık doğrudan gösterilmiş durumda**. “k=1, güçlü bir parametresiz yaklaşım” denebilir; “k=1 özdeşliği doğrulandı” denemez.

**Tek belirleyici sonraki test:** Aynı 1.200 kompozisyon ve aynı hücre yerleşimlerinde, ön kayıtlı **eşleştirilmiş üç koşul karşılaştırması**:

- Mevcut **mpa / omat hacimleri**.
- Yeni **omat / omat hacimleri**.
- Yeni **mpa / mpa’nın kendi Vegard hacimleri**.

Global ve 3/4/5-element katsayılarını, eşleştirilmiş **Δk_model** ve **Δk_geometry** aralıklarını önceden sabitle. Böylece kompozisyon değişmeden model etkisi ile hacim seçimi ayrılır.

**Maliyet:** Yeni omat hedefleri ve iki ikili panel için **5.208**, mpa’nın kendi hacmindeki hedefler için **2.400**: toplam **7.608 yeni K′ hesabı**, saf-element hacim hesapları hariç. Mevcut mpa ikili eğrileri fiziksel hacim üzerinden yeniden sorgulanabilir; grid kapsamı kontrol edilmeli. Ölçülen koşu hızlarıyla **yaklaşık 11 saat**; omat hız farkı ve yakınsama kontrolleri ek süre gerektirebilir. Bu test MACE içindeki ayrımı çözer; fiziksel doğrulama yerine geçmez.

   İkili eğrisi fiziksel olarak `V_ij^omat × exp(dlnV)` hacminde hesaplanıyor; `ln(V0^omat/V_ij^omat)` sorgusu onu **hedefin hesaplandığı aynı V0’ya** getiriyor. Yanlış hacim eşleştirmesi yok.

   Bununla birlikte ölçülen özellik **mpa’nın kendi denge geometrisindeki özellik değil**, omat hacminde clamped eğrilik. Mevcut saf-element sonuçlarında mpa hacim farkı Cu’da **+%0,54**, Pt’de **+%1,24**. Hedefleri yeni hacimde hesaplamadan bunun k üzerindeki yönü/büyüklüğü belirlenemez. Yalnız `V_ij` tabanını değiştirmek de katsayının tanımını değiştirir; sabit hedef hacmindeki parametresiz tahmini değiştirmez.

6. **Hacim transferinin büyük tahmin kazancı sağlaması ayakta.** [k_mpa_equiv.py:99](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:99>).

   İki panel ortalamasıyla:

   | Tahmin | RMSE |
   |---|---:|
   | Pair-at-`V_ij` | **4,8118 GPa** |
   | Hacim transferi, k=1 | **2,2130 GPa** |
   | Aynı veride k=1,138 fit’i | **2,1505 GPa** |

   Parametresiz kural **%54,0 RMSE azalması** sağlıyor ve **934/1.200** kompozisyonda daha iyi. Katsayı fit’inin ek kazancı yalnız **%2,8**; ayrıca bu son sayı eğitim içi, bağımsız doğrulama değil.

7. **Omat’ın aynı hassasiyette k=1’i dışlaması mümkün; mevcut kontrol zaten buna işaret ediyor.** [k_floor_cells.py:103](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_floor_cells.py:103>), [k_floor_cells.csv:2](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/data/k_floor_cells.csv:2>).

Daha güçlü kontrol olan 150 kompozisyon × iki bağımsız omat hedef hücresinde, mevcut ikilileri seed **0 | 1,2** olarak ayırınca **k=1,1065**, koşullu bootstrap **%95 CI≈[1,019;1,201]**. Diğer iki panel bölünmesinde de aralık 1’i dışlıyor. Omat’ta 3/4/5 element katsayıları **1,007/1,187/1,165**: mpa’daki tabakalaşmaya benziyor.

   **Bu, aynı 1.200 kompozisyon ve 3+3 seed tasarımı değildir**; tek-seed panelin belirsizliği bootstrap ile tam öğrenilemez. Dolayısıyla “omat kesin geçerdi” de “mpa–omat farkı kanıtlandı” da denemez. Eski PASS kapıları zaten esas olarak tahmin kazancını sınamıştı.

8. **Güç simülasyonu iyimserdi; yine de bu FAIL’i `design` yapmıyor.** [k_mpa_equiv.py:130](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_mpa_equiv.py:130>).

Kompozisyona bağlı artık hücre ortalamasıyla kaybolmuyor. Bildirilen `%100 power` bu nedenle fazla kesin. Buna rağmen gerçek veriden hesaplanan aralık yeterince dar ve 1’den uzak: burada sonuç yalnız düşük güç yüzünden belirsiz kalmış değil.

**Desteklenen iddia:** İki seçenek arasında **“yaklaşık 1,1 civarında etkin katsayılı hacim transferi”** daha doğru. Fakat “model-dependent” henüz ayrıştırılmış değil; **kompozisyon dağılımına bağımlılık doğrudan gösterilmiş durumda**. “k=1, güçlü bir parametresiz yaklaşım” denebilir; “k=1 özdeşliği doğrulandı” denemez.

**Tek belirleyici sonraki test:** Aynı 1.200 kompozisyon ve aynı hücre yerleşimlerinde, ön kayıtlı **eşleştirilmiş üç koşul karşılaştırması**:

- Mevcut **mpa / omat hacimleri**.
- Yeni **omat / omat hacimleri**.
- Yeni **mpa / mpa’nın kendi Vegard hacimleri**.

Global ve 3/4/5-element katsayılarını, eşleştirilmiş **Δk_model** ve **Δk_geometry** aralıklarını önceden sabitle. Böylece kompozisyon değişmeden model etkisi ile hacim seçimi ayrılır.

Mevcut mpa ikili eğrileri fiziksel hacim üzerinden yeniden sorgulanabilir; grid kapsamı kontrol edilmeli.
